races.name: Norfolk Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Agamemnon
runners_data.note: Ran once at 5f on Good, finishing sixth last time — inconsistent early profile, and though a naturally prominent type, the volume of similar runners in this field means he is unlikely to secure that position cleanly; Ryan Hughes angle warrants watching if he finds cover.

runners_data.name: Blake's Monarch
runners_data.note: Placed at 6f at Sandown last time out after a modest sixth at Ascot over 6f, suggesting he handles Good ground but has questions to answer dropping to 5f; de Sousa rides, and the horse's front-running instincts will be tested by the crowded prominent lane.

runners_data.name: Carry The Flag
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore partners this Aidan O'Brien-trained colt who has form of 1-2-2 including winning at 5f Good — one of the more experienced runners in the field; naturally wants to be prominent and Moore's ability to find a lead rail position gives him a real chance of securing that spot ahead of rivals mapped behind him.

runners_data.name: El Floridita
runners_data.note: Won impressively at 5f Good last time after a moderate debut, and Nigel Tinkler's yard is in form; wants to race prominently but will face strong competition for that role, and Rowan Scott will need a clean draw and quick thinking to avoid being squeezed back.

runners_data.name: Flight Signal
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's 5f winner at Goodwood showed excellent natural pace on Good ground, and James Doyle's positional intelligence is an asset if the horse can find a slot near the front; Watson's juveniles tend to be sharp out of the gates and this horse profiles as one of the most legitimate threats to take an actual prominent position rather than being shuffled back.

runners_data.name: Force Noir
runners_data.note: Won at 5f Good and placed at 5f Heavy — handles quick ground adequately and wears blinkers — but this naturally prominent type has been mapped rearward in this configuration due to overpopulation in the prominent lane; Kevin Philippart de Foy's yard is lightly represented and 54 days since last run adds a fitness query.

runners_data.name: Mr Macartney
runners_data.note: Recent form of 6-7-1-4 suggests inconsistency and his last two runs have been modest after a 5f win at Chester; wears a visor and is a natural prominent runner who is almost certain to find himself without his preferred berth in this congested field.

runners_data.name: Mussab
runners_data.note: Third on debut over 6f at Curragh on Good — one run makes style profiling difficult, and the step to 5f in a Group 2 is a sharp ask; Colin Keane provides the most informative read, but the unknown style and minimal experience limit confidence.

runners_data.name: New Yorker
runners_data.note: The most convincing hold-up profile in the race with a form string of 1-3-4 and Wayne Lordan aboard for Aidan O'Brien — wears a hood and has won at 5f on Soft, with placings at 5f on Good; a genuine closer in a field that lacks true hold-up runners, though Ascot's straight 5f offers only a brief window to deliver a late challenge.

runners_data.name: Orthodox
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's unbeaten juvenile won at 5f Goodwood on Good ground — clean, professional form and Rossa Ryan is a capable partner; as a genuinely prominent type who has won over this trip and going, he has a realistic profile to secure a forward position if the draw allows.

runners_data.name: Persian Spring
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's 6f winner who ran fifth at 5f — Jamie Spencer rides and his front-rank tactical instincts could be valuable here; the drop to 5f is not guaranteed to suit given the 5f form line, but the Good to Firm ground is in his favour.

runners_data.name: Savage Mariner
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand partners this Hugo Palmer second-run juvenile who placed at 6f Good — profiling as an unknown style type mapped to the rear due to field shortfall in genuine hold-up runners; six furlongs may be the natural trip and 5f looks on the sharp side for a second-run horse.

runners_data.name: Social Symbol
runners_data.note: William Buick on a Simon and Ed Crisford-trained winner over 5f Good — sharp profile, exactly the right trip and ground, and Buick's ability to slot just behind the lead from a clean break makes this horse very interesting; the yard is precise with first-time-out winners and this horse has a natural aptitude for the race shape.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Glory
runners_data.note: Charles Hills sends out a 5f winner on Firm and a 6f third on Firm — good ground suits and Jason Watson takes the ride; the horse has placings on similar ground and a compact form profile, though the step to Group 2 is a significant jump.

runners_data.name: Star Prospect
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's charge placed at 3/5f on Good and won at 5f Soft — Dylan Browne McMonagle rides and brings strong Irish juvenile form; the horse wants to be prominent and the jockey will look to find a rail position, making this a credible contender if a slot opens up near the pace.

runners_data.name: Tribeca
runners_data.note: Robson De Aguiar's winner over 6f Good — the step back to 5f and the class leap to Group 2 are both queries, and 56 days since last run is the longest break in the field; Donagh O'Connor rides and the horse's 6f win suggests stamina is its strength, not pure 5f pace.

runners_data.name: Underdog
runners_data.note: Only eight days since his last run — Saffie Osborne partners Richard Spencer's unbeaten 5f winner on Good ground, and the freshness of the prep suggests the yard has targeted this race deliberately; the short turnaround is worth monitoring but the going and trip are squarely in his favour.

runners_data.name: Where Love Lives
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner with two wins from two at 5f Good — Kevin Stott will send her straight to the front and the question is simply whether she can sustain it against 20 rivals; the lack of any genuine pace challenger means she gets the lead uncontested and controls her own fractions.

runners_data.name: Ez Tina
runners_data.note: Wesley Ward juvenile making her turf debut in the UK — going is unknown quantity after racing on a different surface; blinkers suggest she will show early speed, but unknown quantity on Good to Firm turf at a stiff, fast-run Ascot 5f.

runners_data.name: Fanshell Beach
runners_data.note: Another Ward-trained American raider whose European turf experience is nil — James McDonald takes the ride which adds a significant positive, but the going uncertainty and group-race step up from debut are genuine concerns; may show raw speed early.

runners_data.name: Through The Years
runners_data.note: The most experienced of the Ward raiders with a second and a win — John Velazquez takes the ride and brings US Grade-race intelligence to the tactical challenge; going unknown on British turf, but of the three Ward runners this horse's form profile is the deepest.

races.paceDynamic: Where Love Lives is the one confirmed front-runner in a field of 21 juveniles, and with Kevin Stott aboard a two-from-two speedball, she will attempt to set a comfortable, controlled tempo on the Good to Firm Ascot five furlongs — a track that offers no bend and puts a premium on clean breaks and straightforward galloping ability. The paradox of this race is that the field is saturated with prominent-running types — Flight Signal, Mr Macartney, El Floridita, Carry The Flag, Social Symbol, Orthodox, Persian Spring and others all want to be on or near the pace — meaning a large portion of the field will be shuffled into positions behind the leaders that do not reflect their natural running style. This congestion in the prominent positions means pace will be genuine and sustained from the outset, as multiple horses compete for the spots immediately behind Where Love Lives, ensuring no horse gets a truly soft lead. The race shape therefore favours genuine front-runners and any horse with the tactical speed to sit just off the early pressure and sustain a long, flat-out sprint to the line — horses forced deep into midfield roles out of character are significantly disadvantaged.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Clean Lead, Controlled Fractions
scenarios.trigger: If Where Love Lives secures an uncontested lead and the prominent pack fails to close the gap before the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Where Love Lives secures an uncontested lead and the prominent pack fails to close the gap before the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Early Speed War, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the multiple prominent types fight furiously for position in the first two furlongs, burning out the front rank and leaving the race to those who settle just off the pace.
scenarios.body: If the multiple prominent types fight furiously for position in the first two furlongs, burning out the front rank and leaving the race to those who settle just off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Settler Wins Wide
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent-type horse secures a clean position just off Where Love Lives on the stands-side or centre of the track and outstays the pace-pressured runners.
scenarios.body: If a prominent-type horse secures a clean position just off Where Love Lives on the stands-side or centre of the track and outstays the pace-pressured runners.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finisher Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically and the field bunches, allowing any horse coming from the rear to produce a finishing burst.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses dramatically and the field bunches, allowing any horse coming from the rear to produce a finishing burst.

watchPoints.text: Where Love Lives breaks well and dictates — if she crosses to a rail position unchallenged inside the first furlong, she becomes extremely difficult to peg back on fast ground over this straight five.

The prominent lane congestion between Flight Signal, Social Symbol, Carry The Flag and Orthodox in the opening stages will be chaotic — watch for any horse squeezed or checked in the first two furlongs, as positional issues here are race-ending over 5f.

The three Wesley Ward raiders (Ez Tina, Fanshell Beach, Through The Years) all wear blinkers and are unknown quantities on British turf — if any one of them shows explosive early speed, they could disrupt the anticipated pace map entirely.

New Yordan is the only true hold-up horse in the race — Wayne Lordan will likely be last or second last early, and over a straight Ascot 5f on fast ground, the margin for a winning late run is razor thin; monitor how far off the pace he settles.

Several runners carry 54-56 day breaks (Force Noir, Tribeca) or are first-time runners at a new level — fitness and Group 2 experience gaps could result in a larger-than-expected winning margin if the market leaders handle the noise and pressure of a 21-runner Royal Ascot field.

races.name: Hardwicke Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Amiloc
runners_data.note: Won twice at 1m2f-1m4f on Good, including a Listed success, and Ralph Beckett's horses have been firing (7 wins from 48 runners over 14 days); true racing style is prominent, though the sheer density of pace in this field means he is unlikely to get his preferred front-rank berth — that is a real tactical compromise at this level.|

runners_data.name: Best Secret
runners_data.note: French raider trained by S Wattel who has won twice over 1m2f on Heavy/Good in France, though his two soft-surface wins and only two relevant sim-going runs at this track profile are a concern on Good to Firm; he wants to race prominently but will likely find himself squeezed into a midfield role by the traffic, dulling his chance.|

runners_data.name: Ethical Diamond
runners_data.note: Six-year-old for Willie Mullins who has won three of his last five including at 1m4f on Good, wears a hood, and has strong similar-going form (8 from 15 wins or places); comes in on an 84-day break but Mullins is 4/27 over 14 days and DBM is a strong booking — genuine prominent racer who has a realistic chance of actually securing a good position here.|

runners_data.name: Giavellotto
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old Marco Botti stable star with a win at 1m2f on Tapeta and strong course-and-distance profile, placed in 8 of 10 similar-going runs; consistent without winning as often as his rating suggests, and Oisin Murphy will aim to sit just off the pace in a position he can likely hold given his horse's well-established racing pattern.|

runners_data.name: Goliath
runners_data.note: Belgian-trained six-year-old for Graffard who won last time out at 1m2f on Good (just 20 days ago), handles this going extremely well with 8 from 15 sim-going records, and Christophe Soumillon gives him an experienced pilot who will hunt a prominent pitch — arguably the most in-form horse in the race.|

runners_data.name: Jan Brueghel
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner here; Ryan Moore and Aidan O'Brien (9/37 over 14 days) will exploit the solo lead position, and his win at 1m4f on Good plus four wins from nine similar-going runs underpin a strong each-way case — the STYLE_FIT flag reflects that he is the one horse whose role is completely secured, not undermined.|

runners_data.name: Lambourn
runners_data.note: Second Aidan O'Brien runner, also 14 days since his last run; genuinely wants to race prominently but with O'Brien already fielding Jan Brueghel as the designated front-runner, Lordan may find himself further back than ideal — the redistribution to hold-up reflects real positional risk, and his inconsistent going record (SOF/GOO mix) adds mild uncertainty.|

runners_data.name: Phantom Flight
runners_data.note: George Scott's seven-year-old is a genuine prominent-style horse with four wins from 15 similar-going starts but his last six form reads 1-1916, including a poor run at this distance in his most recent outing; excellent sim-going exposure (14 from 15) but the form dip and likely failure to hold his natural position in this traffic-heavy field are both concerns.|

runners_data.name: Sons And Lovers
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien-trained five-year-old whose two wins came at 1m2f-1m5f on Good, and who has strong sim-going numbers (13 from 15), but his last four runs all produced placings not wins; naturally wants to go forward yet is effectively mapped to midfield by the pack of prominent types ahead of him — Boudot will have to make do with a holding role.|

runners_data.name: West Wind Blows
runners_data.note: Simon & Ed Crisford's seven-year-old is a serial placer with 0 wins from 11 similar-going attempts — extraordinary consistency in running second but almost never converts; William Buick will aim to deliver him late as he has been redistributed to a hold-up role that may actually suit his lack of finishing thrust, but the win-less stat at this going is stark.|

runners_data.name: Kalpana
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's five-year-old mare is the one runner carrying a 3lb allowance (126lbs) and has won her last two, both at 1m2f on Good; Colin Keane partners her and she has a strong similar-going record (9 from 15, 4 wins) — if there is a late surge to be had on the straight, her fresh-legged, in-form profile makes her the most dangerous of the hold-up contingent.|

runners_data.name: Santorini Star
runners_data.note: William Haggas-trained five-year-old who has won four of his last five and arrives 30 days fresh; also on 126lbs and has sound form at 1m4f on Good/Soft, but his true nature is prominent and the REDISTRIBUTED tag reflects the likelihood he will be racing further back than ideal — Haggas's horses have been in excellent form (9/41 over 14 days) and this horse's raw ability could compensate for the positional compromise.|

races.paceDynamic: Jan Brueghel is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Ryan Moore aboard for Aidan O'Brien, is highly likely to take this field along at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over 1m4f at Ascot — a track that rewards horses who travel economically and finish strongly. The pace will be honest but not brutal, with Jan Brueghel setting a rhythm that suits his own profile without inviting serious early pressure, and the field behind him is stacked with prominent types all competing for the same real estate: Amiloc, Best Secret, Ethical Diamond, Giavellotto, Goliath, Phantom Flight, Sons And Lovers, and Santorini Star cannot all secure the positions their trainers would prefer, meaning a congested, competitive group will form just behind the leader with several effectively racing against their instincts. This field contains significantly more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — of those pushing for position, Ethical Diamond, Goliath, and Giavellotto are most likely to physically secure prominent berths given their class and recent form, while the others are shuffled further back than ideal. The race shape strongly favours a horse that can travel fluidly in a prominent-to-midfield position, sustain its effort through the rising ground in the straight, and produce a clean turn of foot — making genuine class performers who handle Good to Firm and stay 1m4f well the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jan Brueghel Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Jan Brueghel sets a comfortable solo lead and Moore judges the pace to perfection, arriving at the straight with a decisive advantage.
scenarios.body: If Jan Brueghel sets a comfortable solo lead and Moore judges the pace to perfection, arriving at the straight with a decisive advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to string the field out and a top-class prominent tracker pounces turning for home.
scenarios.body: If the pace is strong enough to string the field out and a top-class prominent tracker pounces turning for home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Finisher Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is brisk enough to compromise those up close and a horse from further back gets a clear run through the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is brisk enough to compromise those up close and a horse from further back gets a clear run through the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — No Clear Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses, several prominent types refuse to settle, and the race becomes a rough-house tactical affair that scrambles the form.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses, several prominent types refuse to settle, and the race becomes a rough-house tactical affair that scrambles the form.

watchPoints.text: Jan Brueghel is the only horse guaranteed a clean, uncontested lead — watch whether Moore takes it up immediately from the gate or allows the first furlong to settle, as any hesitation could see Ethical Diamond or Goliath press into his space and turn this into a contested pace race rather than a controlled solo.

The cluster of prominent types — Amiloc, Best Secret, Phantom Flight, Sons And Lovers, and Santorini Star — all want the same ground in the first half-mile; watch the first two furlongs for bumping, checking, and energy-burning jostling that could compromise multiple fancied runners before the race has truly begun.

Kalpana and West Wind Blows have been mapped to a hold-up role by redistribution but are naturally prominent-leaning — watch whether their jockeys (Keane, Buick) accept the back-of-midfield position or try to push forward early, which would further add to the traffic chaos in the middle of the pack.

Goliath runs just 20 days after his last outing and Soumillon tends to place him positively — watch the pre-race market for any support drift that might indicate the short turnaround is a concern, as he is otherwise one of the more straightforwardly placed horses in a complicated field.

Ethical Diamond arrives on an 84-day break for Willie Mullins wearing a hood — watch his behaviour in the preliminaries and early in the race, as first-time-back horses with headgear can be unpredictable in their early pace commitment, which on a congested Good to Firm track at Ascot could be critical.

races.name: Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Stakes (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Almeraq
runners_data.note: Won last time at Goodwood on Good ground in fine style and William Haggas is in excellent current form; a natural front-runner or prominent racer who is mapped to hold-up here only because the field lacks sufficient hold-up types to fill the rear, meaning it is likely to race at the front of the midfield pack rather than from a genuine back position.

runners_data.name: Aramram
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon runner with solid course-and-distance form including wins on Soft, but his best Good-ground figures are only moderate; inclined to race prominently, though the traffic in this field means he will be further back than he would ideally choose, which the 0.91 style-fit flag reflects.

runners_data.name: Comanche Brave
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's four-year-old won at this track and trip on Good ground last time out and is clearly progressive, but Pierre-Charles Boudot will need to manage a position that is likely to be further back than this horse's natural front-running preference — a key tactical question with 19 runners.

runners_data.name: Great Wish
runners_data.note: Has shown classy form at the top level including a Windsor Castle win, but returns after 84 days off for Bent Olsen; naturally prominent but forced into midfield by the crowded pace scenario, and the layoff combined with a trainer with a single runner in the 14-day window adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Jasour
runners_data.note: True hold-up type for Clive Cox with a tongue-tie, but has finished sixth in five of his last six starts on Good ground at this trip — the form strongly suggests he needs a stronger pace than Satono Reve is likely to set, making this ground and pace shape a concern.

runners_data.name: Khaadem
runners_data.note: Veteran ten-year-old in sprinting, trained by Charles Hills, who won on Firm ground and has some pace figures, but recent Good-ground form reads poorly (9th, 12th) and at this age he requires extreme conditions or an unusually strong gallop to be competitive; pure hold-up style.

runners_data.name: Kind Of Blue
runners_data.note: William Buick on a consistent front-rank performer for James Fanshawe who finished second in a similar race on Good ground last time; maps naturally to a prominent position and this race shape suits him if he can sit close to Satono Reve without burning energy early.

runners_data.name: Lake Forest
runners_data.note: Top-rated at OR 119 and drops back from further trips having won at Haydock; William Haggas/Cieren Fallon a strong combination, and the horse's ability to travel prominently and finish off is a serious asset — the step back to 6f is the key query.

runners_data.name: Lugal
runners_data.note: Japanese raider for Haruki Sugiyama who has placed consistently at the top level on Good ground over 6f at Ascot; 84 days off is a concern, but the form profile at this course and trip is strong and a prominent style suits the likely race shape.

runners_data.name: Overpass
runners_data.note: Australian seven-year-old who ran just four days ago, which is an unusual return; Joshua Parr rides and the horse has consistent placed form on Good ground, but the very short turnaround from his last run is a significant flag for any analyst.

runners_data.name: Powerful Glory
runners_data.note: Jamie Spencer on a Fahey four-year-old who has won twice this season including a York success on Good ground; Spencer's tactical intelligence is an asset in a big field, and if he can pinch a prominent position the horse has the finishing kick to be dangerous.

runners_data.name: Regional
runners_data.note: Consistent Edward Bethell eight-year-old with strong placing record on Good ground at 6f, but is a natural prominent type pushed back into midfield by the volume of pace in this field; Callum Rodriguez rides, and the horse's form shows he needs to race forward to be effective.

runners_data.name: Sajir
runners_data.note: André Fabre runner who has won twice in three starts this year including on Good ground at 6f, finishing second to a top-class rival last time; Oisin Murphy is a key booking and the prominent racing style suits the expected shape well — form points him as one of the most in-form runners here.

runners_data.name: Satono Reve
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, ridden by Ryan Moore who rarely wastes a good tactical position; wears a tongue-tie and has course-and-distance form, winning here last season, and an uncontested lead on Good to Firm ground over 6f is a significant tactical advantage.

runners_data.name: Stolen Kiss
runners_data.note: French raider with three consecutive wins including on Soft; naturally keen to race prominently but will be further back than ideal given the congestion, a factor the 0.92 style-fit flag captures — Good to Firm may also be faster than ideal given those wins came on Soft and Standard.

runners_data.name: Flora Of Bermuda
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's mare won last time at Haydock on Good ground and James Doyle rides; she is a prominent-racer by nature who will need to work hard to secure a forward position in a 19-runner field, and her best Ascot form has been from a handy pitch.

runners_data.name: Joliestar
runners_data.note: Chris Waller's Australian mare has won three on the bounce and is unbeaten in 2025, with victories on both Soft and Good ground; James McDonald partnership is high-class, prominent style suits perfectly, and the form figures make her one of the strongest candidates in the race.

runners_data.name: Sayidah Dariyan
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes filly on 128lbs, returning after 49 days; a natural pace-prominent type who finished third at Newbury on Good last time, but will be deep in the field given the surplus of prominent horses — the redistribution away from her natural position is a genuine handicap.

runners_data.name: Time For Sandals
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace four-year-old who ran just four days ago, and while the horse has some decent form, a recent run at a big-field sprint on Good to Firm with another quick turnaround is a notable concern; maps to midfield due to surplus of prominent types, which is not her ideal position.

races.paceDynamic: Satono Reve is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of 19 and, critically, is unlikely to face any meaningful pressure for the lead on Good to Firm ground at Ascot, allowing Ryan Moore to dictate a sustainable but not suicidal gallop over six furlongs. The pace is therefore moderate-to-honest rather than searching, and with no genuine challenger for the early lead, the front end will not be burned off — giving Satono Reve every chance to control tempo and dictate the race from start to finish. Behind him, a clutch of natural prominent types — Kind Of Blue, Lake Forest, Joliestar, Sajir, Powerful Glory, Overpass and Lugal — will jostle for the handful of positions just off the pace, whilst runners such as Comanche Brave, Regional, Flora Of Bermuda, Stolen Kiss and others who would ordinarily race prominently are effectively squeezed into midfield by the sheer volume of pace-keen horses in this field. This race shape strongly favours horses with the tactical speed to sit in the first four or five and produce a finish from a good position, as there is no strong pace likely to set up the race for closers grinding from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Satono Reve Dictates Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Satono Reve is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and sets a controlled, gallop-friendly tempo that drains the finish from closers.
scenarios.body: If Satono Reve is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and sets a controlled, gallop-friendly tempo that drains the finish from closers.

scenarios.trigger: If Satono Reve sets a pace that just tips over into too-strong, allowing the best-placed prominent horses to sweep past in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Satono Reve sets a pace that just tips over into too-strong, allowing the best-placed prominent horses to sweep past in the final furlong.

scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Emerges

scenarios.body: If the pace collapses abruptly late and creates a late-run opportunity that draws genuine hold-up horses through beaten rivals.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Crowded Midfield Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes early crowding among the many prominent types pushed back, producing interference and an untidy race that opens the door for a fresh rival.
scenarios.body: If the large field causes early crowding among the many prominent types pushed back, producing interference and an untidy race that opens the door for a fresh rival.

watchPoints.text: Satono Reve (Ryan Moore) is the only confirmed front-runner and if allowed a completely uncontested lead on Good to Firm ground, he converts this into a significant race-shape advantage that Moore is ideally placed to exploit.

Overpass and Time For Sandals both ran just four days ago — monitor for any signs of a rushed preparation or market drift that signals the connections are accepting a penalty run rather than expecting peak performance.

With at least eight naturally prominent horses compressed into the midfield in a 19-runner field, watch the first two furlongs for crowding and interference on the stands rail; any horse drawn wide and forced to use early energy to get position will be compromised.

Joliestar (James McDonald) arrives unbeaten in three runs in 2025 and is the most form-boosted runner in the field — watch her market move on raceday as McDonald's booking from the Waller yard for a Group 1 in Britain rarely goes uninstructed.

Sajir's last three runs show 1st-2nd-2nd, and André Fabre's record in British sprints is understated; Oisin Murphy is riding at peak form this season and the horse's prominent style is ideally matched to the likely race shape.

races.name: Jersey Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Dorset
runners_data.note: Ran well at this trip on good and soft for O'Brien but his last two runs (7th, 8th) suggest a horse not firing at his best; a natural front-runner by instinct, he will find himself shuffled back in this large prominent-heavy field and is unlikely to reproduce his Irish form from a compromised position.

runners_data.name: Thesecretadversary
runners_data.note: Stack-trained 3yo with two wins at 7f-8f on good ground and solid course form; races prominently in the traditional sense and should secure a decent pitch in mid-division, though his record suggests a horse who runs honestly rather than one who consistently finds extra when the race quickens.

runners_data.name: Andab
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes over for Joseph O'Brien, and the visor (v) is a noteworthy headgear addition; a consistent runner at 8f on good ground with five places from seven similar-going starts, but his natural prominence means he'll be crowded in traffic early and will need a clear run to exploit the staying power his form suggests he has.

runners_data.name: Ardisia
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's filly has a mixed profile — wins at 7f but has been beaten at 6f and 7f in her last four; consistent enough on similar going (10/15) but her wide-draw vulnerabilities in a big field and a tendency to race prominently in a race overloaded with that profile represents a real positional problem.

runners_data.name: Avicenna
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's unbeaten-at-conditions 3yo (2W from 2 at 7f on good) returns after 49 days; a genuinely prominent horse in terms of natural inclination, pushed rearward only by the maths of this field, and his class and course-trip form deserve respect even though the redistribution note means he may not find his natural rhythm.

runners_data.name: Billecart
runners_data.note: K R Burke's gelding is the truest hold-up type in the race by style, but his form reads 4-150 and he ran 12th last time at 8f on good ground; the going is fine for him but the step back to 7f and the quality of this field make it hard to see him building on a modest recent run.

runners_data.name: Catullus
runners_data.note: William Buick partners a Charlie Appleby horse with two wins at 7f on good — excellent figures (7/7 on similar going, 2W5P) and progressive form; pushed rearward by redistribution but is at heart a prominent racer who may find himself in a better position than his map slot implies, and Buick will be fully aware of that.

runners_data.name: Colori Forever
runners_data.note: Botti's colt has won twice at 7f including on good ground and has been placed at this trip on the all-weather; a genuinely prominent horse squeezed into midfield by this crowded pace map, his course form is modest but his 7f record is strong and any clear run in the straight makes him dangerous.

runners_data.name: Into The Sky
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle sends out a lightly-raced 3yo who won at 6f on good and ran well at 8f; Oisin Murphy takes a mount that looks like a genuine pace-securing type who shouldn't struggle for position in this race, and a step up to 7f looks entirely within range.

runners_data.name: Morris Dancer
runners_data.note: The Gosdens' horse is the sole confirmed front-runner and returns after a very long layoff (311 days); his two wins came at 7f-8f on good and his form before injury was smart, but the fitness question mark following nearly a year off is significant and must temper any assumption he'll dominate as comfortably as his role suggests.

runners_data.name: Neolithic
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore and A P O'Brien — a combination that speaks for itself at Ascot; wears a hood (b) and has won at 6f and 7f including on soft, with a solid record on similar going (4/6), and Moore's ability to read a race from a prominent position makes this one of the more interesting rides in the field.

runners_data.name: Saber Strike
runners_data.note: William Haggas and Tom Marquand send out a horse who is 2W2W — unbeaten in two starts at 7f and 6f on good ground; the sample is tiny but the form is perfect and Haggas horses often arrive at Royal Ascot fitter than they appear, making the 50-day absence less alarming than it might be for others.

runners_data.name: Take Charge Star
runners_data.note: Murtagh's colt wears a hood (t) and has one win at 7f on good from six similar-going runs; a prominent type by nature who is likely to find himself shuffled back in this traffic, and his recent form (8th, 5th, 2nd, 6th) does not inspire confidence that he'll make his way through from a compromised position.

runners_data.name: America Queen
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes' filly is lightly raced but has won at 6f on good and been placed twice at 7f; Billy Loughnane rides and she carries 126lbs as a filly which is a slight weight advantage — her profile says prominent and competitive, and she should be close enough to matter if the race develops cleanly.

runners_data.name: Domina Ignis
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy's filly won at 6f on good but ran 18th at 8f and 3rd at 7f in her last two — a wide spread of form; a natural front-runner in style who is functionally mapped to midfield by the field's composition, and her recent consistency is not strong enough to suggest she'll work through the pack effectively.

runners_data.name: Green Sense
runners_data.note: James McDonald takes over for Joseph O'Brien on a horse who has won at 6f on soft but whose form at 7f and beyond on good ground is more mixed (6th, 11th in last two); a prominent horse by inclination who finds himself in a midfield slot by redistribution, and form figures of 0-1-3-0-6 suggest this is a horse who finds one or two too good rather than one who wins a big race.

runners_data.name: The Prettiest Star
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's filly is the highest-rated of the fillies in the race (OR=109) and has won at 6f before finishing 2nd at 7f and 4th at 8f; James Doyle rides and her form progression — three runs, three solid efforts on good ground — suggests a genuinely progressive type who should secure a prominent position naturally and whose class could make her competitive late.

races.paceDynamic: Morris Dancer is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with a field of 17 largely prominent types jostling for early position, he is likely to dictate from the front without a genuine pace rival to press him — the question is whether that pace is fast enough to stretch the field or slow enough to bunch it. Into The Sky, America Queen, Neolithic, Saber Strike, and The Prettiest Star are the horses most likely to sit in the slipstream just behind Morris Dancer, forming a tight, competitive pocket through the first half of the race. The field is overloaded with prominent-running types — Dorset, Andab, Ardisia, Colori Forever, Green Sense, Domina Ignis, Take Charge Star, and Avicenna are all natural prominent/near-prominent horses who have been redistributed into midfield or hold-up slots purely because there is no room for them at the front in a 17-runner field; the horses most likely to actually secure prominent berths are Into The Sky, America Queen, Neolithic, and Saber Strike given their stronger pace credentials and simpler profiles. With one uncontested pace-setter controlling tempo on good-to-firm ground over 7f at Ascot — a track that rewards horses travelling strongly into the straight — the race shape strongly favours hold-up horses and genuine closers who can switch off, travel efficiently mid-pack, and produce a powerful sustained finish, though the reality that few confirmed hold-up types exist in this field gives prominent racers who track the pace cleanly a major tactical edge.

scenarios.body: If Morris Dancer sets a deceptively slow early gallop that compresses the field and leaves little time for closers to deliver a finishing burst.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Bunch Kick, Pace Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is just strong enough to string out the field but Morris Dancer weakens inside the final two furlongs, gifting the finish to mid-pack prominent types.
scenarios.body: If the early tempo is just strong enough to string out the field but Morris Dancer weakens inside the final two furlongs, gifting the finish to mid-pack prominent types.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If Morris Dancer sets a genuinely strong gallop that burns off mid-pack rivals and leaves the race open for hold-up horses to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: If Morris Dancer sets a genuinely strong gallop that burns off mid-pack rivals and leaves the race open for hold-up horses to pick up the pieces.

watchPoints.text: Morris Dancer's fitness after 311 days off is the single biggest swing factor in this race — if he comes home tired in the last furlong, the entire pace map inverts and the scenario probabilities shift dramatically toward tracking types who conserved energy behind him.

With 13 of 17 runners tagged as prominent types, the first two furlongs could see significant jostling for position — watch for Ardisia, Domina Ignis, and Take Charge Star in particular, who risk being shuffled wide or back early if the field breaks quickly.

Saber Strike is unbeaten but has run only twice; if William Haggas has targeted this race with a genuinely ready horse, the minimal form makes him very hard to assess — Tom Marquand's positioning from the early stages will be the clearest read on whether the stable thinks he's ready to compete.

Catullus and Avicenna are both pushed to rear-field map positions by redistribution despite being prominent horses at heart — watch whether Buick and Dawson attempt to push forward from their stalls early, which would confirm their natural inclination and change how the race shape reads.

The going report confirms Good To Firm for the 7f race despite a Flat card description — horses with soft-ground wins in their profiles (Neolithic, Andab, Dorset) should be assessed primarily on their good-ground figures, where their records are noticeably less dominant.

races.name: Wokingham Stakes (Heritage Handicap)

runners_data.name: Spy Chief
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter here; Buick will bowl along in front and with no immediate rival to push him, the question is whether his Good to Firm form at six furlongs — solid but not dominant — is good enough once the closers arrive; note the STYLE_FIT flag suggests he's racing slightly out of role as he's naturally a prominent rather than pure front-runner.

runners_data.name: Soldier's Tree
runners_data.note: De Sousa partners this consistent prominent type for James Owen, who is 9/50 over the last 14 days; limited similar-going form (just 1 win from 4) but recent form string reads 3-123 and a front-rank position is guaranteed in this shape — gives him a clean run.

runners_data.name: Run Boy Run
runners_data.note: Wore hood last time; off 84 days which is a flag in a 6f sprint handicap, and his recent form includes an 11th at this track — needs everything to fall right, though a previous 1st at 5f on Good underlines his ability on quick ground.

runners_data.name: Double Rush
runners_data.note: Won back-to-back on Good ground at 6f and sits perfectly into this pace map as a genuine prominent type who should secure his natural position; Shane Foley is in excellent form (12/57 T14) and Andrew Balding's yard is firing.

runners_data.name: Mitbaahy
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse who will sit last and wait; Billy Loughnane rides for Charles Hills, whose yard has been relatively quiet (2/13 T14), and Mitbaahy's similar-going record is patchy (2 wins from 10 sim-going efforts) — though he won a Haydock Listed over 6f on Good, the big field suits late runners if pace collapses.

runners_data.name: Binhareer
runners_data.note: Won at 6f on Good in May for William Haggas, who remains in strong form (11/30 T14); Tom Marquand retains the ride and Binhareer's recent form (2361-2) shows consistent involvement — a genuine prominent type who should get his position cleanly.

runners_data.name: Two Tribes
runners_data.note: Off 106 days and blinkers fitted; recent form has tailed off (5-1200) after back-to-back wins, and similar-going record of 2 wins from 15 efforts on Good suggests the ground may blunt his best form — stall position and freshness are the questions.

runners_data.name: Heathcliff
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon rides this prominent type trained by James Fanshawe; only 1 run on similar going from 15, which is a significant concern — most of his form comes on Tapeta or artificially watered surfaces, and the Good to Firm ground here may catch him out.

runners_data.name: Dubai Bling
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes over for Hugo Palmer (8/35 T14), and Dubai Bling's form on Good ground is excellent including a 6f Newbury win in April; prominent-racing and well drawn to get a clean position, this is one of the more interesting profiles in the race.

runners_data.name: Royal Zabeel
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby sends this 5yo out on 42 days' rest; similar-going record of 1 win from 7 on Good and a recent 5th at 7f is not compelling — a prominent type who may find 28 runners and a stiff Ascot track tough to negotiate.

runners_data.name: Leovanni
runners_data.note: James McDonald takes the ride for K R Burke (9/50 T14); off 119 days which is noteworthy for a 6f handicapper, and his form at 6f on Good — mostly 5f wins — suggests the trip or the long break could be against him, despite the top-class jockey.

runners_data.name: Hammer The Hammer
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's yard has been quiet (2/36 T14) and Hammer The Hammer's last run was a 0 (last) — the visor has appeared previously; prominent type who needs a kinder pace and a cleaner passage than this field is likely to offer.

runners_data.name: Caburn
runners_data.note: A genuinely prominent-racing horse who is almost certainly going to find himself further back than he wants in this field; Colin Keane is capable of manufacturing a position but 28 runners at Ascot over 6f will make that difficult — the STYLE_FIT flag is a real concern here.

runners_data.name: Roman Dragon
runners_data.note: Carries a ⚠ fade warning and the form includes some poor similar-going runs (14/15 sim-going efforts); Mason Paetel takes the 5lb claim and the horse ran just 14 days ago — the tendency to weaken in the closing stages is a clear negative in a sprint that favours finishers.

runners_data.name: Flash Harry
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan partners this 4yo for Clive Cox (2/16 T14), and his natural style is to press the pace — but in this field he's likely to be pushed back from his preferred spot, and with a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.90 the redistribution is a genuine handicap to his chance.

runners_data.name: Fandom
runners_data.note: Sean Levey rides the recent winner for Richard Hannon (9/44 T14) who is in good order; Fandom's last run was just 20 days ago and he won at 6f on Good, but he is a natural prominent type who will struggle to secure that position in this field — the redistribution undercuts what looks a live form angle.

runners_data.name: Far Above Dream
runners_data.note: Four wins from nine on similar going is an outstanding strike rate for James Owen's yard, which is in rampant form; Kieran Shoemark partners and the form reads 101-11, but the honest note is that this prominent type is very likely to be shuffled back from his natural position in a 28-runner field, which compromises what is otherwise a strong profile.

runners_data.name: Ten Pounds
runners_data.note: Jamie Spencer is patient enough to adapt his tactics; Joey Ramsden sends this 5yo out on 21 days' rest with recent form of 2 at 5f on Good — a natural prominent type who will find life harder than usual in a field this deep, though Spencer's race-reading may help.

runners_data.name: Completely Random
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore is aboard for Harry Charlton (2/16 T14); the horse won back-to-back on Standard at 6f, not on Good turf, and his similar-going record of 1 win from 9 is moderate — Moore will do what Moore does but the ground form is a gap.

runners_data.name: Thunderbear
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse for Jack Davison, whose yard has had zero winners from 5 starts over the 14-day period; Thunderbear won at 6f on Good and his hold-up style is authentic, though he needs a pace collapse and clear daylight to be at his best.

runners_data.name: Candy
runners_data.note: Off 259 days — the longest absence in the field — for Richard Spencer; a 4yo who has shown ability on Soft ground but whose form on Good (17th and 20th in two starts) is poor, and the long layoff makes confidence difficult even with Saffie Osborne's experience in the saddle.

runners_data.name: Fast Track Harry
runners_data.note: Jack Nicholls (5) takes the claim for Clive Cox, who has two runners in this race; the form reads -11770 and the horse won twice on Standard ground at 6f but not on Good turf — squeezed further back than natural by the large field, this is a tough assignment.

runners_data.name: Apollo One
runners_data.note: Christophe Soumillon takes over on this 8yo hold-up horse; ran 14 days ago and recent form of 082939 tells a story of inconsistency — only 2 places from 9 similar-going runs and the age has to be a question in a highly competitive sprint like this.

runners_data.name: Evening Saigon
runners_data.note: Callum Rodriguez partners for Hamad Al Jehani, a small yard (4/9 T14); form of /10-12 includes two wins on Standard/Soft ground — this is a natural prominent type who finds

races.paceDynamic: Spy Chief is the one confirmed front-runner and, in a field of 28, is likely to get a clear lead without being seriously pressured early — William Buick will dictate a sustainable gallop from the front, setting a honest but not suicidal pace on Good to Firm ground over six furlongs at Ascot. The field is saturated with natural prominent types — Far Above Dream, Fandom, Flash Harry, Caburn, Evening Saigon, Realign and others all want to race close to the pace but simply cannot all occupy those positions in a 28-runner sprint, meaning several will be shuffled back into unfamiliar midfield territory. The race is therefore likely to develop into a two-furlong dash from the two-pole, with the inside and centre of the track both in play as jockeys hunt the best ground. This shape — a controlled lead, a compressed midfield, and a genuine test of finishing speed in the final furlong — most strongly favours horses who genuinely race prominently or can travel smoothly in the first wave, and those redistributed hold-up types who find clear daylight soonest; of the front-runners likely to secure their natural position, Double Rush and Dubai Bling profile best, while Spy Chief, Binhareer and Soldier's Tree also fit the pace map cleanly.

races.name: Golden Gates Stakes (Handicap)

runners_data.name: Bourbon Blues
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse in natural style, handled well by Joe Leavy for Brian Meehan; solid recent form with a win and two places in last five, all good ground runs look encouraging at this trip and the 35-day break appears straightforward.

runners_data.name: Sahara King
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner and sole pace-setter here, James Doyle gives this a big chance to dictate; the [STYLE_FIT] flag is relevant — this horse is vulnerable if the tactical picture changes around it, but its role as lone leader is valuable in itself.

runners_data.name: Evanesco
runners_data.note: David Egan partners this prominent type who won over 10f on good ground last time for Charlie Johnston; the step back here from a 48-day break looks straightforward and his form figures on good ground (1,4,6) are acceptable at this level.

runners_data.name: Spyce
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan takes the ride on this Alan King-trained prominent racer whose recent form shows a flat stretch on good ground at this trip; four runs at 10f on good ground have returned one win and limited improvement, the pace bottleneck may squeeze him wider than ideal.

runners_data.name: Bayaann
runners_data.note: William Haggas's lightly-raced three-year-old arrives off just 12 days' rest after winning on debut at this trip, and Cieren Fallon's booking is strong; only three career starts but all three suggest a horse with a proper turn of foot, the key question is whether handicap company at this level comes too soon.

runners_data.name: Nil Bua Gan Dua
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle partners this JPO'Brien-trained prominent type who has consistently placed on good ground at this trip; five runs at 8-10f on good ground have returned one win and three placings — consistent and reliable, well placed here.

runners_data.name: Harmonics
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's three-year-old has won two of his last three including a 10f good-ground win that reads well for this; Shane Foley's booking adds interest and the 15-day turnaround appears unconcerning given that recent run freshness.

runners_data.name: Sunset On Leros
runners_data.note: Marco Ghiani rides this hold-up horse who has placed twice on good ground at shorter trips for Marco Botti; the headgear flag (hg:p) is worth noting, and the 50-day absence is the mildest concern, but this horse has shown it can settle and deliver off a genuine pace.

runners_data.name: Balzac
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam's three-year-old is naturally a prominent racer but the packed pace map means Billy Loughnane will likely find him absorbed into midfield — his best form comes at 8-12f on good ground with three placings, and the [STYLE_FIT] tag appropriately tempers expectations if he cannot race forward.

runners_data.name: Amadeus Mozart
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the mount for Aidan O'Brien on a horse whose true character is prominent, though the competition for early position makes that difficult here; won over 7f and placed at 10-12f, the soft-ground form (2nd over 12f) adds a minor uncertainty on fast going.

runners_data.name: Lost Boys
runners_data.note: James McDonald partners this consistent three-year-old who has won his last two over 10f on good ground for David Menuisier — his natural prominent style is likely to be squeezed by the congested pace, but McDonald's strength through the straight could compensate if he can find a position close enough.

runners_data.name: Allegresse
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy partners this hold-up type for Andrew Balding who is in strong form (12/57 in 14 days); recent form has dipped but good-ground placed runs are on the card, and the 14-day turnaround is no concern for this stable.

runners_data.name: Perisher
runners_data.note: William Buick's mount is naturally a prominent racer who won two of his last three including a 10f good-ground win — the crowded pace map redistributes him to midfield, which Buick is capable of managing, but his best form clearly comes when able to race with cover close to the pace.

runners_data.name: Princling
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand rides this William Haggas-trained three-year-old whose four-race record shows one win and two places, all at 7-8f on good or standard ground — the step up to 10f is a key question for a horse pushed into midfield by the prominent traffic; the stable form is strong.

runners_data.name: Folk Pageant
runners_data.note: Rowan Scott partners this progressive Charlie Johnston runner who has won four of his last five including three consecutive wins at 10f on good and soft; a genuine prominent type whose recent dominance at this trip is eye-catching, but the congested pace map means he is unlikely to race where he wants.

runners_data.name: Echo Of Stars
runners_data.note: Jamie Spencer takes the ride for Oliver Cole on this horse who won over 10f on good ground last time; naturally a prominent type, the headgear (hg:t) is noted, and his [STYLE_FIT] tag reflects the challenge of racing out of position — Spencer's tactical nous could be an asset if he can slot comfortably.

runners_data.name: Accredit
runners_data.note: Non-runner — listed for reference only; John & Thady Gosden's three-year-old with 246 days absent, irrelevant to the pace map here.

races.paceDynamic: Sahara King is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival for the lead, James Doyle should be able to dictate a controlled, measured gallop from the front in this 1m2f handicap on Good to Firm ground at Ascot. The pace will be sustainable rather than scorching, meaning the tempo is unlikely to dramatically compress the field or shred the field mid-race, creating a race shape that rewards horses able to travel comfortably close to the pace and produce a clean turn-of-foot in the straight. This configuration — a lone leader setting a fair but manageable gallop — classically favours prominent racers and mid-division types who can slot in behind the pace without burning fuel, then quicken over the rising Ascot ground. The field holds significantly more front-running and prominent types than can realistically get their natural position: Balzac, Amadeus Mozart, Lost Boys, Perisher, Princling, Folk Pageant, and Echo Of Stars are all genuine prominent horses who will be shuffled wider or deeper than ideal — of those, Lost Boys, Amadeus Mozart and Perisher are most likely to push closest to the front in the early stages given their stronger recent form and jockey profiles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sahara King Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Sahara King dictates a comfortable lead and sets a pace that keeps the race honest but not brutal, allowing prominent horses who do secure a position to travel sweetly.
scenarios.body: If Sahara King dictates a comfortable lead and sets a pace that keeps the race honest but not brutal, allowing prominent horses who do secure a position to travel sweetly.

scenarios.label: B

scenarios.body: If the congestion of prominent horses causes early jostling and forces a stronger pace than Sahara King intends, creating a more strung-out race from the outset.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely fast enough through the middle sections to string the field out and leave leaders vulnerable, handing hold-up horses momentum in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely fast enough through the middle sections to string the field out and leave leaders vulnerable, handing hold-up horses momentum in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Grinding Attrition Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just moderate enough that the race becomes a sustained battle of stamina through the straight rather than a sharp quickening contest.
scenarios.body: If the pace is just moderate enough that the race becomes a sustained battle of stamina through the straight rather than a sharp quickening contest.

watchPoints.text: Sahara King's ability to control the early gallop is the single biggest determinant of the race shape — watch whether James Doyle is allowed to slot quietly to the front or whether Lost Boys, Amadeus Mozart or Folk Pageant push up alongside in the first two furlongs and force a sharper early pace.

Lost Boys and James McDonald are dangerous if McDonald can manoeuvre forward in the early stages despite the crowded pace map — two consecutive 10f good-ground wins make this horse a genuine threat if it gets any closer to the action than midfield.

Harmonics must be monitored in the market and on the track — back-to-back wins including a 10f good-ground win with Gosden/Foley is a combination that can produce sharp performers, and any drifting in the betting here would be a significant negative signal.

The early stages past the start could be physically congested with multiple prominent types all seeking the same ground behind Sahara King — watch for any bumping, crowding or horses having to check in the first two to three furlongs, particularly around Balzac, Perisher and Princling.

Bayaann's fitness and capability at this level on just 12 days' rest and three career starts warrants monitoring — William Haggas is capable of placing horses precisely, but this is a significant step into handicap company and any sign of greenness in the preliminaries should be noted.

races.name: Queen Alexandra Stakes (Conditions Race) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: A Piece Of Heaven
runners_data.note: Progressive stayer with a win and two placings in last three, travels prominently and has strong sim-going form (3W6P on similar ground); eight-year-old holding form well for O'Brien/McMonagle and the step to extreme trip suits his profile.

runners_data.name: Berkshire Sundance
runners_data.note: Has won twice at 16f on Tapeta and returns to turf where his recent form is thinner; genuinely wants to race close to the pace but with several others seeking the same position, he is likely to be shuffled into a role wider and further back than ideal, which tempers his chance.

runners_data.name: Carlton
runners_data.note: A dual winner at up to 2m and capable of front-running, but in this field the crowded prominent ranks mean he is likely to find himself racing against his nature in midfield; headgear suggests he needs holding together, and the drop from his OR peak may reflect diminishing returns.

runners_data.name: Columbus
runners_data.note: Mullins runner returning from 244 days off (40 jumps runs bridging), and his flat form is largely at 12-15f; stepping massively up in trip and fitness from a long layoff are genuine concerns, even for a classily bred horse, and the prominent types crowding him out only compound the challenge.

runners_data.name: Dallas Star
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer who has placed in six of his recent starts without winning; runs out of his natural rear division position legitimately and is suited by a strong gallop, which makes him most dangerous in Scenario B rather than the likely Scenario A.

runners_data.name: French Master
runners_data.note: Gosden/Doyle combination, won over 14f on Good ground and has strong sim-going record (8/10); races prominently and has the class (OR 108) to sit just off the pace and quicken, making him a prime beneficiary of Illinois setting a controlled tempo that he can stalk.

runners_data.name: Hipop De Loire
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with blinkers applied, genuinely wants to race prominently, and is one of the most likely candidates to press Illinois for the early lead; recent form is modest (7th, then question marks in form string) and if he softens the race up he may help others more than himself.

runners_data.name: Illinois
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with Ryan Moore aboard, which implies a controlled rather than suicidal lead; OR 111 makes him top-rated and his two second-place finishes over 16-20f on Good suggest he stays well, though STYLE_FIT flag notes he is in an unusual role for this type of race shape.

runners_data.name: Le Destrier
runners_data.note: Buick/Mullins hold-up horse returning from 36 days off with limited sim-going evidence (2/4); best form at shorter trips (12-14f) and asking him to settle and close over 2m5½f is a significant test, though the stable angle and jockey booking maintain interest.

runners_data.name: Maxi King
runners_data.note: Placed in five of last six, runs from an honest prominent position and has decent sim-going form (5/15); De Foy handler has him fit from 43 days off and the consistent placing record makes him a reliable each-way profile in the stalking scenario without being a dominant winning candidate.

runners_data.name: Mr Hollywood
runners_data.note: Mullins hold-up horse returning from 269 days off (40 jumps runs bridging); best form is over shorter trips on soft, and the combination of genuine layoff, quicker ground than preferred, and an extreme distance is a considerable ask even accounting for a powerful stable's ability to produce them fresh.

runners_data.name: Aajej
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a headgear note (hg:p) and no sim-going wins from nine attempts on similar ground; OR 77 is the lowest in the field bar Pivotal Days, and while a win at 14f on Standard suggests ability, the step to 2m5½f in a deeper conditions race looks a significant jump.

runners_data.name: Pivotal Days
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner (OR 63) and a genuine hold-up type mapped to midfield due to redistribution pressure; five-run form string shows no win and only one placing, and the long layoff (105 days, jumping bridge) combined with a drop back to turf and an extreme trip makes a significant impact very hard to envisage.

races.paceDynamic: Illinois is the one confirmed front-runner in a 13-runner field over 2m5½f at Ascot on Good to Firm ground, and with Ryan Moore aboard he is likely to be allowed to bowl along at a controlled, measured tempo rather than being harried into suicidal fractions. The field contains a cluster of horses whose natural preference is to race prominently — Hipop De Loire, Berkshire Sundance, Carlton, Columbus, French Master and Maxi King all want to be on or near the pace — but the map cannot accommodate all of them, and several will be pushed wider or further back than they would choose; Hipop De Loire and Berkshire Sundance are the most likely candidates to press Illinois and at least partly dictate terms, while Carlton and Columbus are likely to be frustrated into a mid-division role they do not naturally inhabit. At this extreme distance on quick ground, a steady-to-moderate gallop set by a single, unflustered pace-maker strongly favours horses who can travel smoothly in the first half, preserve energy through the long middle section, and then produce a sustained run rather than a sprint — making prominent-to-midfield stalkers with strong Good-to-Firm form the chief beneficiaries, while true closers who need a genuine end-to-end test are disadvantaged by the lack of forcing fractions.

watchPoints.text: Illinois (Ryan Moore) sets all the fractions unchallenged — if he bowls along at a comfortable clip and is never headed, horses who cannot travel prominently are racing for minor honours before the home turn.

Hipop De Loire and Berkshire Sundance both want to be prominent and could crowd Illinois in the first mile — monitor whether their presence forces a quicker-than-expected pace that changes the race shape entirely.

Columbus and Mr Hollywood both return from very long breaks (244 and 269 days off, bridged by jumps runs) — stable confidence in both Mullins entries is worth noting, but fitness after such absences at this extreme trip on fast ground is a live concern.

French Master's jockey change to James Doyle (high-profile booking) at OR 108 with strong Good-to-Firm form makes him the most naturally positioned beneficiary if Illinois controls the pace — watch how early Doyle commits him turning for home.

Le Destrier carries the Buick/Mullins pairing and has placed on only 2 of 4 sim-going runs; his hold-up profile is genuine but the trip extension from recent 12-14f form means whether he truly stays 2m5½f on fast ground is unresolved and a key unknown in the race.
